blockingLoop.evidence: Repeated 'please check if the rinse aid level is low' and 'try running an intensive 65°C programme' after the customer had already said both programmes came out cold, but the customer still got to the resistance test

rationale: The assistant eventually reached the correct hidden truth: it had the customer isolate power, measure across the heater terminals, correctly read the open circuit as a failed heater integrated into the circulation pump, and framed repair vs replace on a 9-year-old machine with an engineer option. However, it wasted two turns on an irrelevant rinse-aid check and re-asked for the 65°C test after the customer had already reported both programmes cold, and one turn was lost to a service error. Terminology ('flow-through heater', 'both parts') was slightly muddled and no actual heat-pump part or cost guidance for this model was given, but nothing unsafe or fabricated appeared.
